title: Reported As Hiten P. Dalal vs . Bratindra Nath Banerjee on 15 February, 2010
full_text: Reported As Hiten P. Dalal vs . Bratindra Nath Banerjee on 15 February, 2010 IN THE COURT OF SH. ANAND SWAROOP AGGARWAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE-CUM-RENT CONTROLLER PATIALA HOUSE COURTS, NEW DELHI Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (Old) 2552/1/05 Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (New) 4679/1/09 M/s Precision Testing Machines Pvt. Ltd. S-12, Okhla Industrial Estate, Phase-II, New Delhi -110020 ........Complainant Versus Sh Rajiv Gupta, Proprietor Raj Motors,Near Rajapur Pul-Petrol Pump Patna-I (Bihar) ........ Accused A. Date of institution of the complaint : 16.11.2005 B. Date of conclusion of final arguments & fixing the matter for orders : 15.02.2010 C. Date of Judgment : 15.02.2010 D. Final Order : Convicted u/s 138 N.I. Act. COMPLAINANT UNDER SECTION 138 r/w SECTION 142 OF THE NEGOTIABLE INSTRUMENTS ACT, 1881. JUDGMENT 15/02/2010 This complaint under Section 138 of the N.I. Act, 1881 has been filed with the averments that the Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (Old) 2552/1/05 Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (New) 4679/1/09 1/14 complainant company M/s Precision Testing Machines Pvt. Ltd.,S-12, Okhla Industrial Estate, Phase-II, New Delhi -110020; is an existing Company registered under the Companies Act,1956 , having its registered office at S-12, Okhla Industrial Area, Phase-2, New Delhi-110 002 and it is engaged in the business of marketing of Shophisticated Authomotive Diagnostic and Body Shop Equipment etc. This complaint has been instituted and filed through Sh. S. C. Gupta, Officer of the complainant company, who has been empowered by the Board of Directors of the complainant company to be authorised representative of the complainant company to institute, file, sign, verify, as well as prosecute and conduct the complaints under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 , and also under the provisions of the Indian Penal Code , 1860, vide Board resolution passed in the meeting of Board of Director on 12.05.2005. As alleged Mr. S. C. Gupta, Authorised Representative is also well conversant with the facts and circumstances leading to the filing of the present complaint on the basis of the record made available by the concerned Departments of the Complainant Company. Further, as alleged by the complainant, accused is a proprietor of Raj Motors and accused placed order on the complainant company for supplying Low Temperature Drier Plant and Wheel Alignment Machine. The complainant Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (Old) 2552/1/05 Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (New) 4679/1/09 2/14 company supplied the said equipment/machineries to the accused and, as per the terms of the order, the balance consideration of Rs.2,07,228/- of the said machineries/ equipment was to be paid by the accused by demand draft, payable at New Delhi, at the time of taking delivery of the said machineries/equipment. However, when the complainant's representative reached with the consignment of the said equipment/machineries, the accused instead of making payment of the balance amount through a demand draft, requested to accept cheque bearing No.234764 dated 30.09.2005 for Rs.2,07,228/-. The complainant company accepted the same on the assurance of the accused that the said cheque is good for payment and would be honoured by accused's bankers upon presentation by the complainant company. But on presentation the said cheque was dishonoured & returned unpaid by the banker of accused on account of INSUFFICIENT FUND in the accused's bank account vide returning memo dated 03.10.2005 giving the reason for the dishonour of the cheque as "Payment stopped by Drawer". Thereafter, complainant sent a legal notice dated 08.10.2005 to the accused under the provision of section 138(b) N.I. Act through its advocate through Regd. A.D. post & UPC on 08.10.2005. As alleged, the legal notice sent to accused through registered A.D. Post & UPC have not been returned back & therefore it must have been served upon the accused on or about 13.10.2005. Further, it is alleged, that even after Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (Old) 2552/1/05 Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (New) 4679/1/09 3/14 receipt of legal notice accused has neither replied the notice nor paid the amount against the dishonoured cheque and thus accused has committed an offence punishable under section 138 NI Act r/w section 142 of NI Act 1881 r/w section 420 IPC. 2. Vide order dated 12.12.2005 accused was summoned to face trial for the offence under section 138 NI Act. 3. On 25.05.2007 notice under section 251 Cr.PC was framed against the accused to which he pleaded not guilty. 4. To substantiate its case on judicial file, complainant has examined Mr. S.C. Gupta as CW1. On 28.07.2009 CE(post notice) was closed by ld. counsel for the complainant. On 19.08.2009 statement of the accused was recorded under section 313 Cr.P.C. Accused intended to lead DE and has examined one defence witness namely DW1 Mr. Vinay Prasad Arya. On 30.10.2009 accused closed defence evidence. 5. I have heard Sh. Manoj Kumar, Adv. for the complainant and Sh. Chakravarty Pal, Adv. for accused and gone through the case file very carefully. Ld. counsel for the complainant has submitted that receipt of the statutory demand notice has not been disputed by the Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (Old) 2552/1/05 Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (New) 4679/1/09 4/14 accused. As submitted, till date cheque amount has not been paid by the accused & this complaint has been filed with prescribed period of Limitation. Further, it is submitted that delivery of the goods is also not disputed by the accused. On the other hand ld. counsel for the accused submitted that accused had got prepared three demand drafts & payment was supposed to be made at the time of delivery of goods. It is further submitted that on 08.10.2005 instruments/goods were taken back by complainant & thus notice given by complainant had become infructuous & no cause of action further survived for the filing of this complaint case. Further, it is submitted that accused had paid Rs.2 lacs in cash to Mr. Shivraj Shenoy on 26.07.2005 at Patna alongwith two Demand drafts for total value of Rs.62,5000/- & thus the cheque in question was issued as a security and not in discharge of any debt/liability. 6. I have given a considered thought to the rival submissions made by ld. counsel for the parties, keeping in view the facts and circumstances of this case as they arise from the material available on judicial file. 7. Undisputedly accused Mr. Rajeev Gupta is proprietor of M/s Raj Motors & he had placed an order to the Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (Old) 2552/1/05 Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (New) 4679/1/09 5/14 complainant company for supply of Low Temperature Drier Plant and Wheel Alignment/equipment. Accused admittedly had received the demand notice Ex. CW1/9. As per accused it was duly replied. But reply has not been placed on record. Further, undisputedly accused received the said machine on 29.09.2005 and transporter had demanded a sum of Rs.2,07,228/- from the complainant. As per accused, he had already paid a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- in cash on 26.07.2005 to Mr. Shivraj Shenoy, Regional Manager of Eastern Region of the complainant company and thus transporter was made to have talks with Mr. Shivraj Shenoy & he (Mr. Shivraj Shenoy) had further asked the accused to give a cheque of Rs.2,07,228/- as a security, so that the transporter may deliver the goods as per order placed by the accused and thus goods were delivered to accused as per instructions given by Mr. Shivraj Shenoy. As such undisputedly cheque in question has been issued/executed by accused. As per statement made by accused under section 313 Cr. P.C all the contents of the cheque have been filled by the accused. In these circumstances to my mind, presumption under section 139 N.I. Act can be safely drawn in favour of the complainant and against the accused in as much as admittedly the cheque in question was issued in favour of the complainant against supply of equipment by the complainant to the accused. Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (Old) 2552/1/05 Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (New) 4679/1/09 6/14 Now, since execution of the cheque has been admitted by the accused, presumption u/s 139 NI Act is to be mandatorily drawn in favour of the complainant & against the accused. However, this presumption is rebuttable; to be rebutted by the accused. Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in a case law reported as Hiten P. Dalal V/s. Bratindra Nath Banerjee (supra) has observed as under : " 24 ...................................... .......................The more authoritative view has been laid down in the subsequent decision of the Constitution Bench in Dhanvantrai Balwantrai Desai v. State of Maharashtra where this Court reiterated the principle enunciated in State of Madras v. Vaidyanatha Iyer and clarified that the distinction between the two kinds of presumption lay not only in the mandate to the court, but also in the nature of evidence required to rebut the two. In the case of discretionary presumption the presumption if drawn may be rebutted by an explanation which "might reasonably be true and which is consistent with the innocence" of the accused. On the other Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (Old) 2552/1/05 Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (New) 4679/1/09 7/14 hand in the case of a mandatory presumption " The burden resting on the accused person in such a case would not be as light as it is where a presumption is raised under Section 114 of the Evidence Act and cannot be held to be discharged merely by reason of the fact that the explanation offered by the accused is reasonable and probable. It must further be shown that the explanation is a true one. The words 'unless the contrary is proved' which occur in this provision make it clear that the presumption has to be rebutted by 'proof' and not by a bare explanation which is merely plausible. A fact is said to be proved when its existence is directly established or when upon the material before, it the court finds its existence to be so probable that a reasonable man would act on the supposition that it exists. Unless, therefore, the explanation is supported by proof, the presumption created by the provision cannot be said to be rebutted"." Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (Old) 2552/1/05 Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (New) 4679/1/09 8/14 Now I have to see whether in this case, accused has been able to rebut the presumption raised in favour of the complainant & against the accuse under section 139 N.I. Act. To rebut the presumption, accused is supposed to prove that he as a matter of fact had paid Rs.2 lacs in cash to Mr. Shivraj Shenoy at Patna. The stand of the accused is that he had given two DD's for total value of Rs.625000/- to Mr. Shivraj Shenoy at his workshop M/s Raj Motor's at Patna alongwith a sum of Rs.2 lacs paid in cash to Mr. Shivraj Shenoy. But, as per, complainant, advance payment of Rs.625500/- through two DD's were given by accused himself to complainant company at Delhi office of complainant company vide Ex. CW1/5a. As per complainant as sum of Rs.10,000/- was given in cash to accused as desired by him vide debit advice Ex.CW1/5(b). As regards Ex.CW1/5a, accused in his statement recorded under section 313 / 281 Cr.P.C. has stated that "I cannot say anything about Ex. CW1/5a." The said Ex. CW1/5a is dated 6/08/2005 and it also bears the signature of the accused dated 6/08/05. By giving abovesaid reply to Ex. CW1/5a, accused has, by necessary implication, can be said to have admitted the letter dated 6/08/2005 Ex. CW1/5a. He has not disputed his signature on Ex. CW1/5a. Accused has not further controverted the stand of the Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (Old) 2552/1/05 Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (New) 4679/1/09 9/14 complainant that a sum of Rs.10,000/- was returned in cash to the accused by the complainant. As regards Ex. CW1/5b, the debit advice, accused has stated that "I do not remember whether Ex.CW1/5b have been signed by me". Further accused has stated that "I do not remember whether I received Rs.10,000/- as short term loan, as deposed". Again accused is not disputing his signature on debit advice Ex.CW1/5b. Thus in the facts & circumstances of this case it can be said that this court can rely upon Ex.CW1/5a and Ex.CW1/5b as proved/admitted/undisputed documents. In Ex.CW1/5a it has been specifically mentioned that net advance received by complainant towards purchase order of the accused is Rs.6,15,500/-. The said letter is dated 6/08/2005. Now, one fail to understand as to why accused silently signed the said letter dated 6/08/2005 without making a protest regardings Rs.2 lacs having already been paid to Mr. Shivraj Shenoy on 26/07/05 in cash towards the purchase order in question. Accused has not placed on record any communication made by him to the complainant company regarding cash payment of Rs.2 lacs allegedly made by accused to Mr. Shivraj Shenoy on 26/07/05. Also depositions made by DW1 Mr. Vinay Prasad Arya does not appear to be trust worthy in the facts & circumstances of this case. This witness appears to have deposed in the court as per sayings of Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (Old) 2552/1/05 Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (New) 4679/1/09 10/14 the accused himself. He has deposed that he did not know Mr. Shivraj Shenoy prior to 26/07/05. Further he has deposed that he had not himself seen the DDs allegedly given by accused to Mr. Shivraj Shenoy. Also this witness could not tell in whose favour the said DDs had been issued. Further this witness could not tell about the total numbers of DDs. Also, as deposed, this witness had not counted the cash of Rs.2 lacs allegedly given by accused to Mr. Shivraj Shenoy. Also this witness in his affidavit has not deposed that accused had introduced DW Mr. Vinay Prasad Arya with Mr. Shivraj Shenoy. Also DW1 Mr. Vinay Prasad Arya had not taken any visiting card of the person to whom, as alleged, accused had given Rs.2 lacs nor any identity proof of such person was given by said person to DW1 Mr. Vinay Prasad Arya. DW1 Mr. Vinay Prasad Arya has specifically deposed that he believed that the person to whom payment was made was Shivraj Shenoy because it was so told to him by the accused. Thus it can be said that DW1 Mr. Vinay Prasad Arya has deposed on the basis of hearsay as was told to him by accused. Also depositions made by DW1 Mr. Vinay Prasad Arya appear to be quite improbable in the facts a circumstances of this case. DW1 Mr. Vinay Prashad Arya is himself not a customer of accused & he simply used to visit the workshop of accused with his friend as and when there was necessity of service of vehicle owned by his Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (Old) 2552/1/05 Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (New) 4679/1/09 11/14 friend. This witness DW1 has specifically deposed that besides his relationship with the accused as a customer there is no relationship of friendship or other relationship with the accused. Further DW1 has deposed that accused never used to share his business & family matters with him. Thus it is quite improbable that, in these circumstances, accused would introduce DW1 with Mr. Shivraj Shenoy or will tell the DW1 about payments made; as alleged, by accused to Mr. Shivraj Shenoy. As regards the circumstances in which cheque in question was accepted by the transporter from the accused CW1 Mr. S.C. Gupta has deposed that request was made by accused to receive the said payment by cheque in as much as he (accused) could not get prepared the DD for the said sum as agreed. Thus much importance cannot be attached to the factum that on the Challan Mark B it was mentioned as under :- " Driver mall khali karne say pahle party say Rs.2,07,228/- ka DD langa phir mall khali karega." Further as per accused goods/equipment was delivered to accused as per the instructions given to the transporter by Mr. Shivraj Shenoy. But accused has neither examined Mr. Shivraj Shenoy nor the transporter Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (Old) 2552/1/05 Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (New) 4679/1/09 12/14 whose all details are very much available on Mark B in his defence to substantiate his defence on Judicial file. Further in his application u/s 227 Cr. P.C. in para 4, accused has stated as under :- " 4. That it is pertinent to mention here that the applicant/accused had issued the cheque as per the direction of the complainant that as and when the cash payment would be made the aforesaid cheque could be return." The above stand of the accused is not consistent with the stand taken by accused in the course of his trial. Above stand also suggest that accused was under liability to pay the cheque amount to the complainant. Also in the present case, liability of accused to pay the cheque amount to the complainant had arosen with the delivery of the equipment to the accused & the fact that subsequently heads of the alignment machine for the purposes of calibration and charging the same were taken by complainant does not in any way affect the liability of the accused with regard to cheque in question. At the time cheque was given by accused, accused was under liability to pay the cheque amount to the complainant & Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (Old) 2552/1/05 Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (New) 4679/1/09 13/14 this much is sufficient to make the accused suffer liability u/s 138 N.I. Act. In view of above detailed discussion, in my opinion it can be concluded that accused has failed to rebut the presumption u/s 139 N.I. Act 1881. Accused has failed to prove that he had paid a sum of Rs.2 lacs in cash to Mr. Shivraj Shenoy on 26/07/05 & the cheque was given as a security only. In my opinion in the totality of facts & circumstances of this case, accused is liable to be convicted u/s 138 N.I. Act & it is order accordingly. Let accused be heard on Quantum of Sentence. Pronounced in open court. (Anand Swaroop Aggarwal) SCJ-Cum-RC/New Delhi 15.02.2010 Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (Old) 2552/1/05 Complaint Case (u/s 138 NI Act ) No. (New) 4679/1/09 14/14
